Representative_Docs: ['linguistics major for non-traditional student? also accommodations? hey everyone, i’m a non-traditional/older-than-average student (29 yo), and i’m thinking about finishing a bachelors degree at unc. long story short is that i graduated from wake tech with an associate of arts, then took a couple of years off and afterwards went to nc state but didn’t finish. i’ve since moved from raleigh to chapel hill. tried going back to nc state to finish this year, but it didn’t work out between the drive and my mental health issues/getting things straightened out with my medication. i guess i have a bunch of possibly unrelated questions, haha. 1) is the linguistics department at unc good? i’m interested in hearing from both current students and people who have graduated. for graduates, have you had luck getting jobs in a related field after graduation? i’m particularly interested in teaching english as a foreign language but am open to other options. 2) how is unc for older students? i’m fortunate enough to live near campus, but i have to work to pay my rent and things like that. is the school at all understanding of students who want to be part time so they don’t get overwhelmed between school and work? are there online options for classes, especially in the linguistics department, or are the classes mainly in person and during the day? 3) is unc actually good and understanding about disability accommodations? i’m autistic and have adhd and multiple mental illnesses, so that’s affected my ability to complete classwork on time before. i had accommodations at nc state for these things, so i could probably get them at unc too. however, i’m interested in hearing people’s experiences about whether the disability services at unc are good and whether the professors tend to be understanding about disabilities, particularly mental health issues. sorry for the wall of text, and thank you to anyone who takes the time to answer this. it’s okay if you can only answer one question; any information i can get is helpful. hope everyone has a great semester!', 'congrats on getting in!! i hope you\'re proud of yourself, and definitely hope you choose carolina to be your home. it\'s awesome here. i\'d be happy to talk to you more about business/cs here in dms. 1. even though a lot of my friends got in, they weren\'t the same gender as me (dorms are required for first-years and they\'re all same-sex rooms) so i reached out to people via the unc class instagram page. i lived with some cool people that i still keep in touch with today so i would definitely recommend going a bit outside your comfort zone and reaching out to people you think you\'d vibe with. 2. i\'d say the gyms are good for free ones. when they\'re busiest depends on what you\'re using - wait time for machines is usually short throughout the day, and some facilities may be reserved at times for clubs, classes, or sports. otherwise i\'d say you could go at any time. 3. it\'s honestly not that bad - lenoir is generally agreed to be better than chase, especially since it has two parts (restaurants on the first floor, they accept meal plans/flex money, and traditional dining hall on the second floor). 4. it\'s not a "bad idea," as they\'re degrees that make a lot of sense together and a lot of people do it - but they\'re both hard to get into. a good backup plan to have is statistic & analytics, econ, and information sciences. 5. yes, i brought my switch and my roommate brought her xbox, plus i know a lot of gamers bring their computers here. it\'s a much more reliable option than library computers or the gaming arena in craige. 6. it depends what you\'re looking for. do you want to be social and live alongside the majority of the freshman class? hojo, ehaus, and craige are your best bets. does the thought of waking up at 7:45am and walking to your 8am class on time appeal to you? one of the north campus dorms might be a better fit. 7. i\'m very involved on campus, so the majority of my friendships were made through clubs and activities. i\'d recommend for you to try to make a friend in every class - not only is it an easy way to make friends, it\'s also super useful if you ever need anything in your academics.', 'i mean it’s only four real classes, and some people have tried doing five classes like this. (on the other hand you wouldn’t have room to drop a class.) but aside from that, this is about as tough a schedule as one could come up with for first year. the physics being 9 am doesn’t help either. [i’d like to think i am a pretty good student overall, and the one time i had a 9am class i got a 69 on the final. not even a hard class. would never even think about doing physics at 9.] i would keep only the class for your major, whichever one that is, and find some lighter classes to fill out your schedule. maybe keep 110 if you are really interested or considering the major, but not just bc it “looks good” or something like that. edit to add: i’m not the expert on chem stuff here but if you really know your stuff from gen chem i wouldn’t take 102 again. yes it’s a review, but as you said, it’s a weed out. if it were me i’d rather just go ahead and take orgo than take a class over and probably lower gpa further. that could be a full a filler class instead, whereas you’d be very lucky to get away with an a-/b+ in one of those.']

Name: 0_class_classes_just_school
Representative_Docs: ['everything is not hopeless if you can\'t get a research position your freshman year. for example, the structure of the old curriculum for the biology major made it where most people did not start biol 395 until the second semester of their sophomore year. you can get a research position via cold-emailing professors, however getting to know them directly (or indirectly) is a better option. taking and excelling in a class with a professor can help you get a research position with their lab. you will also want to be active in the classroom by asking good questions/providing good answers. you can also do the same with a professor that knows them (if they research similar things, they probably know each other. if they are co-authors on a paper they definitely know each other). you can talk to your class professor about your interest in doing research with professor x, and ask if they could help you out by putting in a good word/etc. saying your majo research interests/career interests may help people provide bette specific advice. also, it\'s worth considering that some people will "overhype" their positions. it will sound like they are curing cancer and flying spaceships in their second semester, when the reality of their work is mundane.', '1. it\'s not "over for you". you don\'t need research experience as a freshman. the majority of people are not doing research their freshman year. hell, the old biology major track made so that the vast majority of freshmen could not do research their freshman year. 2. i am assuming you have looked at reus, which all state something along the lines of "we encourage applications from underrepresented populations and those at institutions with little/no undergraduate research opportunities". the important part of that is "encourage". you are still eligible to apply for most reus and you have a chance at being accepted (although reus are very competitive). 3. most freshmen do not get summer research internships. i didn\'t even bother applying to any after my freshman year. if you want to feel productive during summer break, you could take a summer class or two at unc (or at a nc community college). the community college route is useful for general education classes, as a graduate admissions committee isn\'t going to care that you took intro to jazz at a community college instead of unc. summer classes are a good way to lighten your load during the regular semester, allowing you to focus on major classes and research. if you don\'t want to take a summer class, look into learning how to code or improving your coding skills. there are many free online resources. unc students have free access to linkedin learning which provides courses on many common programming languages. pretty much every lab nowadays has a need for someone who can code (even if it is just making simple graphs).', 'as a senior i want to just let you know that this happens a lot more than people realize, and while everyone that gives the advice of “attend events” and “leave ur door open to talk to people on ur hall” etc. mean well and are right (it really is the best advice) it’s also important to remember that it is absolutely okay, and normal, to just not make good friends for a bit. it took me like a year and a half to find my actual close friends in college, while i still like everyone i ended up hanging out with freshman year, we didn’t click super well or hangout all the time, just once in awhile. just stick with it, keep talking to people in class (even the upperclassmen), and going to events and clubs. and reach out to people you meet at events, especially other freshman! people are going to these events for the same reason you are: to make new friends. odds are they want someone to reach out to them and ask to hangout just as much as you do, everyone is just too scared to put themself out there first. the worst they can say is no, and even then you’ll probably never see them again so who cares. finally, while it is normal to feel lonely at the beginning of college, it’s important to use your support system to keep it from really impacting your mental health or routine. get out of your dorm everyday, even if it’s by yourself. call home often if you have a good relationship with your family, call your extended family, even if you usually don’t, and keep in touch with friends or teachers from high school! if it really starts to impact you, and you are starting to feel depressed, definitely reach out to caps to get yourself some more help. they have talked to students like yourself countless times, and can help a lot. i did not do this as a freshman when i needed help, and it really did impact my enjoyment of my year as well as my grades— i really regret it so don’t repeat my mistake.']

Representative_Docs: ["no heat in dorm and freezing all night, aren't they supposed to turn it on? weren't they supposed to start turning on the heat in dorms a few weeks ago? i remember receiving an degrees in my room right now.", 'alum here. i’ve been to dublin! it’s a beautiful city. chapel hill is much smaller than dublin but it has a decent share of restaurants and bars/pubs and shops. we can get similar weather as dublin but it doesn’t usually rain as frequently but rains heavier. if i’m looking at the data right we actually average a good bit more annual rainfall than dublin does but that’s because we get more at one time and heavier rain. looks like the dublin airport averages 758mm/29.34in annually. the rdu airport in nc averages 46in/1168mm annually. we get a lot of thunderstorms in the spring and summer and can get the occasional tornado watch which means conditions are right for a tornado to develop. rarely do we get an actual tornado. the coast can get hurricanes in the summer and early autumn but they don’t usually reach here beyond some wind and rain. we do get a good bit of sunshine all year round too. more sunny days than cloudy or rainy days. we average around 111 sunny days and 106 partly sunny days for over 200 days a year with some sunshine. if you measure in daily hours of sunshine chapel hill averages 2600 hours of sun vs 1424 in dublin. right now it is colder in chapel hill than it is in dublin. just checked the weather app. it’s an overcast day and the weather app says it’s going to rain at about 11am in chapel hill for an hour. but we are coming out of a cold spell here where daytime highs barely got above the freezing point for a couple of days. it’s expected to warm up into the 60s/70s (15-20c) and be damp and rainy and overcast by the end of the week. that’s pretty standard winter in nc. might snow or ice or might be rainy and dreary or might be sunny and warm. you just never know in the winter. in the summer it’s always dependably hot and humid and very sticky steamy like you just got out of a hot shower. it’s just a matter of exactly how hot it is in summer. for your purposes of a school term we can start getting summer like days in march where it’s really hot and sunny or it might snow in march. who knows? april will have more hot days and a some warm and pleasant days but spring is short here and we go full on summer usually by may. enough about the weather! you might be able to get a single room but sharing a bedroom with a roommate is the norm in all us universities. chapel hill is a great example of a “college town” in the us. i would definitely encourage you to come if you can. try to make friends who have a car (lots of students have cars) who can take you to the nc beaches or mountains or up to washington dc. public transport outside of the biggest metropolises like new york city is not great. you could catch a bus or train somewhere but it is definitely not the norm. outside of the northeast i’d guess 90% of people in the us rely on cars to get around. that said chapel hill does have a nice free bus system so you can hop on a bus and get to other parts of town "advice needed: showers connected to my room wall causing constant overwhelming noise in dorm room hi! i'm a freshman, living in mcclinton, and i’ve been having issues with constant noise from the showers/electrical closet next to my room. one of my wall’s is connected to both the showers (hall style bathroom) and the electrical closet. thus, whenever someone turns a shower on, my wall emits a high-pitch frequency, accompanied by a loud buzz noise (like 'eeeee'). it permeates my entire room, so it’s hard to ignore or drown out. it also amplifies when multiple showers are on at once, making it sorta sound like construction is happening right next to me. i know that to most people, this noise may simply be bothersome, however, the reason i needed my current room (a single room in a north campus dorm as an accommodation from ars) was due to my anxiety-induced sensory issues around excessive noise. therefore, this constant loud noise triggers the very thing me and my doctors worked hard to try to avoid through getting accommodations. i've found it hard to fall asleep at night, or try to do work in my dorm room, as my floor (of nearly thirty people) takes showers at all times of day/night. i’ve been experiencing sensory overload/crying almost every day i've been here because whenever i walk into my room, or try to relax, the shower noise is overwhelming. so far, i’ve tried anc headphones, foam ear plugs, as well as noise-protection ear muffs (made for construction workers), yet the high-pitch noise still bleeds through. i told my ra about it, who said her community director told her there was nothing they could do, and only offered to give me ear buds (which as i've said, i already tried). i'm not sure what to do from here, and i feel a bit helpless. i don’t want to seem entitled/whiny by asking for a more comfortable living space after i’ve already been accommodated for my disorders, but i don’t think i can live with this constant noise for the entire school year. that all said, i’d deeply appreciate any recommendations on what to do! i’d love to know if anyone has been in a similar situation, if anyone knows who else i could talk to about this, if there’s anything i can do myself to help parr the noise, or, more headphone/earbud recommendations. thank you for reading, and thanks in advance for your help! tldr: advice needed—dorm room wall is connected to the showers which cause a loud construction-like noise constantly, that exacerbates my existing sensory issues."]

Representative_Docs: ['guns don’t kill people. people kill people. this is not a gun issue. it’s a mental health issue. we need to get to the root of the problem here. but liberals are deadset intent on taking away everyone’s guns. that won’t do anything. bad people will still get their hands on guns, and then there won’t be any good people with guns to protect everyone else. it’s a lose lose situation.', 'the problem is your entire comment is based on speculation and hypotheticals, but there’s no need for that. we have a ton of data both in the us and overseas that shows gun control does work. almost all of the states with the lowest gun deaths are blue states with restrictive gun control, and the states with the highest gun deaths have the most lax gun control. look at massachusetts as an example. highest population density in the country, multiple large, diverse cities- and still low gun deaths and violent crime rates because they have some of the strictest gun laws in the country. i don’t disagree that “we have to cut the problem at the source” and more gun control wouldn’t completely eliminate all gun-related problems, but the data shows it would help substantially.', "okay riddle me this.... let's not ban guns because people will find the guns anyway and hurt people. going off of that logic: let's not have nuclear weapon laws because people will find nuclear weapons and hurt people anyways? we clearly have not had nuclear war in a while because of the stricter laws. let me be clear, nobody is targeting the right to safety. it isn't about taking rights away. it's about increasing safety for everyone. if taking the guns out of the hands of these mentally unstable individuals can reduce the number of people who die everyday due to gun violence, then i'm for it, and so are the others arguing against gun laws. 100% let's work to fix mental health issues. 100% let's target the 8 other heads of the hydra, but your analogy is lacking in that it assumes the other 8 heads also kill people at the same rate as the head we're trying to cut off. in more simplistic but graphic terms, if someone threatened you with a weapon, would you be focusing on providing them with therapy in that moment while they have a weapon to your face or trying to get the weapon out of their hands and then get them to therapy? now multiply that by the number of gun violence incidents in the country and you'll understand why it's imperative we get the guns out of people's hands first, then address the other concerns. is stricter gun laws and gun control going to solve the problem completely? no! but will it help reduce the number of innocent children dying on a classroom floor? absolutely. gun control invariably means less children dying, and i am for it. the point i think most people miss is questioning why there even is a need to have guns in civilians' hands? how are there other countries that are getting by without this? why do they have less school shootings than us? aren't we supposed to be the greatest country in the world with the mightiest military? why do americans then not feel safe? we're clearly doing something wrong. and if the current standard of gun control is continuing to place guns in the hands of individuals who shouldn't have them, and if you agree with me that these individuals shouldn't have had a gun in their hands and shouldn't have been able to take the lives of innocent people, then i think something needs to change. and we do that by not continuing to support the status quo. hope that makes sense."]

Name: 15_dei_trump_covid_2025
Representative_Docs: ['you understand dei existed before the supreme court struck down affirmative action? dei is meant to not show racial biases when it comes to any form of recruitment. the sc ruling against affirmation action with unc and harvard said that the consideration of race in admissions to colleges and universities violated the u.s. constitution\'s promise of equal protection under the law. this is because what affirmative action did was they set quotas to admissions. e.g. we have to have 10% admission of one race so out of all the applicants we need to recruit the top people of one race if possible until the total amount reaches 10% of the student population. the difference is dei would blind people\'s race/name or any identifying information so that people\'s race would not be known when being considered for admission. aa tries to set quotas while dei tries to eliminate (mostly negative) biases. i already mentioned in other posts what dei was supposed to do, which is to eliminate biases when a recruiter sees a foreign name, what college they graduated from, what race they are, how old they are, etc... we may have laws that supposedly outlaw that but it\'s near impossible to prove that you were eliminated from a job interview because of your race/name/age/etc... this link here tells you the difference between affirmative action and diversity(or dei). "diversity is not a policy or program but rather a broader concept that emphasizes the value of different perspectives, experiences, and backgrounds."', 'these people can’t even define what dei is. they think it’s the same as affirmative action. i see posts all the time of them blaming “dei” whenever a person of color makes a mistake in their public job saying they would not have been hired if it wasn’t for dei. this is not what dei is, at all. dei programs were meant to make those under-represented groups to feel more represented. they were created to try and remove/reduce implicit biases within people. we’ve all heard the stories of people applying for jobs and how they get less interviews/callbacks when they use a foreign name vs when they use an “american” name. this shouldn’t be a thing. why do foreigners have to change their birth names just to “fit in”? some companies have blinded resumes(removed identifying information) to get rid of these biases so that a person would only be judged based on their job qualifications/education rather than their name or race. growing up as an asian in america has been such a “weird” experience in that, we’re not asian enough to be with people of our own race(those that came from the mainland) but we’re not white enough to be with americans. this isn’t an isolated incidence, many asian americans can relate to this. how we grew up feeling like we never fit in with some group. dei initiatives give us a platform to talk about our experiences and for the non-minorities, a viewpoint into the shit we had to deal with. it’s not surprising those with no empathy don’t care about these things.', 'trump doesn’t have a “project 2025” so….']

Name: 26_mask_people_look_wear
Representative_Docs: ['i hear that :/ i had very similar experiences in school, to the point that if anyone is laughing in my vicinity, i instinctively assume it’s about me, which is rly hard to shake since in the past that has been what’s happening, and because being able to realize that has historically helped me sort of protect myself. the main reason i said it probably doesn’t have anything to do with you is that in college, ppl are so much better at minding their own business lol, and in my experience they - if nothing else - at least want to be subtle if they’re talking about someone. personally, i’ve definitely been in a friend group before that is acting dumb/saying dumb things, and cracked up when we passed/made eye contact with a person because we’re imagining how we must look to them. when i’m by myself, i often instinctively look at the people i’m passing, especially is there’s any kind of visual interest (brightly colored hair, tattoos, etc) because deep down i am just a little creature. i don’t want to invalidate what you’re saying, because ultimately you know your experiences best, but if there’s any room for doubt, those are some things that could be happening. in the event that they are laughing at you—easier to say this from my side, i know, but screw ‘em. it’s a cliche thing to say, but anyone who’d publicly ridicule or laugh at someone on the street because they don’t meet their personal aesthetic standards must genuinely just be so boring, vain, and malicious. if nothing else, you might have a better time taking the bus or walking down columbia to get to weaver street market or harris teeter for groceries—i always found that route less crowded and stressful than franklin. 💖', 'first, i want to say that i’m really sorry you’re dealing with this. i can imagine this is pretty distressing, and i’d be upset too! i’m also really sorry that it’s impacting where you feel comfortable walking. it sounds like everyone is jumping to anxiety, which is certainly possible. (i had a friend who used to express somewhat similar sentiments, and ultimately it was a product of mental health in his case. but he is just one instance.) but also people can be mean (especially college guys) and no one here has been walking with you, so i don’t think anyone should be able to confidently rule out the possibility that these people are just simply being awful. it’s hard to do anything about passing strangers being mean, especially if they’re whispering so you can’t respond directly. i would maybe recommend walking with headphones in/listening to things and just focusing on walking/looking straight ahead. it doesn’t change other people’s behavior, but it should at least shift your attention and provide distraction! and i know it might sound silly, but just some self-assuming mantras could also help your confidence in yourself so that you’re less fazed. like maintaining personal confidence and dismissing the opinions of random college guys and strangers who ultimately don’t matter can just make life easier in general! on the subject of caps, i don’t tend to recommend them. i have personally only seen them once for a short meeting that was mandatory to obtain a psychological withdrawal, but i have had a few friends who have had bad experiences and one who even said her experience with caps kind of exacerbated her mental health crisis. this was a few years ago, so perhaps things have changed, but my understanding is that they really only do well with counseling for things like acute interpersonal issues (the only good reviews i’ve heard are from friends who sought help after a bad breakup or a roommate issue). i know therapy can be expensive though, so if it’s something you decide you’re interested in, then i would recommend searching for someone who does sliding scale payments. sometimes therapists even offer pro bono, so that’s definitely worth reaching out about as well. i hope things get better, op. tl;dr: people can be mean, so headphones and self-reassurance can be your friend on these walks! i don’t recommend caps, but local therapists might have sliding scale or pro bono options that would make therapy more accessible!', "i'm sorry this is happening to you. i've been wearing a mask in crowded areas and in class (indoors and outside) for both my health and others' health. i see a few others in my classes wearing masks. thankfully, i have never been made fun of or seen my classmates been made fun of, though i have been privy to heated debate on both sides. having went maskless for a good portion of last semester for other reasons i won't get into, i understand peoples' desire to wear and to not wear a mask. it is no more acceptable to make fun of someone for wearing or not wearing a mask than it would be acceptable to make fun of someone for something else. i also just wanted to say thank you for being considerate of others' health at this time. i hope you are feeling better now. feel free to let me know if you need anything and i can try my best to help!"]
